title: I Applied the Pipe-Organ Blower Hours to the Organist Who Camped Our Numbered Manual

parts.text: I stepped into the loft at 6:03 p.m. and organist Hale was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE CONSOLE. NINETY MINUTES. BLOWER STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was thirty-two, choir accompanist, holding a clipboard that listed our hymn set. Hale shrugged. "Organists are the loft." I photographed the board, the booking, and his leftover pistons on our numbered manual. Then I asked for the blower log. At 6:11 the sexton pinged why Hale's name was on our wind. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The sexton can see Hale's leftover pistons on our numbered manual.

social.video_title: He camped our numbered manual on our blower hours — Part 1/2
social.description: Pipe organ loft, leftover pistons, a ninety-minute clock he posted. I logged the wind. Would you have asked for the blower log?

parts.text: Hale called it practice coupling until the sexton asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the piston still. The blower went back to our numbered hours. Hale ran a slot of his own and told the next organist atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: ORGANISTS ARE NOT THE LOFT. I keep our pistons on a labeled tray. Hale brown-bags his coupling. The console finally looks like a hymn set, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Organists are not the loft — Part 2/2
social.description: Blower log, numbered manual, and a second line on the board. Was practice coupling ever our wind?
